title: Closures, tasks, and async races
outcome: Predict JavaScript ordering and prevent old requests from replacing new results.
cue: Start order is not finish order.
version: Portable JavaScript · React hooks · Vue 2/3 comparisons · Next App Router

trace.title: Event and stack
trace.detail: JavaScript code runs on a call stack. Browser events and timers schedule later tasks. Promise callbacks use a microtask queue, which is drained after the current stack before the next task. A zero-delay timer means “eligible later,” not “run now.”

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Write the synchronous lines first: A and D. Then drain the promise callback: C. Then the timer task can run: B.

For search, label each request with a number. Only the latest number may publish rows. Also guard loading/error updates; a stale failure must not replace the current success. Encode user input when putting it into a URL.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: await pauses that async function, not the whole browser. A long synchronous loop still blocks input. A stale request can also clear the current loading spinner if only result assignment is guarded.
